kb_version: Microchip AT24CS01 datasheet (DS20006330A), SOIC-8 "SSHM" package variant

provenance.authored_by: hand-transcribed from Microchip AT24CS01 datasheet pin-description table by Nelson (class-1 authority per CLAUDE.md KB-authoring doctrine); NOT derived from the datasheets_parsed Haiku cache or any PDF read by CC
provenance.agreement_gate: 3-way: (a) human-verified datasheet pin table (authority), (b) datasheets_parsed/AT24CS01-SSHM-B/auto/AT24CS01-SSHM-B_pin_groups.json Haiku cache (cross-check: 'Serial Clock Input (SCL)' / 'Serial Data Bidirectional (SDA)' groups), (c) jetson-agx-thor-baseboard top-level .net U54 KiCad symbol pin names (cross-check) — all three agreed pin 5=SDA, pin 6=SCL, no disagreement on pin IDENTITY. Note: U54's actual board wiring swaps these nets (a pre-existing corpus defect, already caught by check_i2c_coherence via pin_function independent of this KB entry) -- that is a WIRING fault, not a disagreement about which silicon pin is SDA vs SCL, and did not block this gate.

i2c_note: AT24CS01 is a fixed-function I2C EEPROM (1 Kbit, 128x8), not an MCU alt-fn mux. SDA/SCL are single-purpose silicon pins -- no possible_roles menu, function_class=fixed applies to them specifically. Per the interim protocol-pins-only standard (adopted after the INA219 landing's STOP #2 -- see kb/vendor/ti/INA219AIDCNR.json provenance.a0_a1_decision), address/config/strap pins (A0, A1, A2, WP) are deliberately NOT KB'd here regardless of their board wiring -- no schema affordance exists yet for 'known, intentional, non-participating bus pin'. On jetson-agx-thor-baseboard (U54) these four pins are all tied to GND, not to any bus net, so this landing carries no STOP-2-shape churn risk from them.
